This is a systematic review, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. The review assesses effectiveness and cost-effectiveness rather than presenting original diagnostic accuracy data with 2x2 tables.

This is a systematic review of NAAT tests in urine specimens, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating a rapid POC test. The review synthesizes data from 29 studies rather than presenting original 2x2 data.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating the Biostar Chlamydia OIA (rapid POC test providing results in <30 min) in women at an STD clinic. Compares OIA with cell culture, DFA, and PCR. Reports sensitivity (73.8%) and specificity. All 306 participants received multiple assays including the index test and reference standards. Provides 2x2 data for diagnostic accuracy.
This is a prevalence survey measuring STI rates in a population, not a diagnostic accuracy study. No POC test is evaluated; only NAAT and serological tests are used to determine infection prevalence.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating rapid POC tests (ACON NG/CT duo, QuickVue Chlamydia RT) in symptomatic women aged 14-49. Pregnant women excluded. Sequential sampling at health clinics. Compares POC tests with NAAT. Reports sensitivity (22.7-37.7%) and specificity (99.3-100%). All participants received both index test and reference standard. Provides 2x2 data.

While Clearview EIA is a rapid test, this study primarily compares multiple laboratory-based diagnostic methods (PACE 2, AMP CT, LCx amplification assays). The focus is on comparing amplification technologies rather than specifically evaluating a rapid POC test. Clearview EIA had unacceptably low sensitivity (50%).

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating the BioStar Chlamydia OIA (rapid POC test) in adolescent women. Uses two different NAATs as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (59.4%) and specificity (98.4%). All 261 participants received both index test and reference standard. Provides 2x2 data.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating the Chlamydia Rapid Test (CRT) POC device in asymptomatic men. Compares with BD ProbeTec ET PCR Assay as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (20%) and specificity (100%). All 100 men received both rapid test and PCR. Provides 2x2 data.
This is a prevalence study using only PCR to determine infection rates. No rapid POC test is evaluated or compared. Does not present diagnostic accuracy data or 2x2 tables.
This is a review article/guideline discussing laboratory diagnostic approaches. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. No original data or 2x2 tables presented.
This is a surveillance study measuring STI prevalence in vulnerable populations (FSWs, MSM). Not a diagnostic accuracy study. No POC test is evaluated.
This is a prevalence/epidemiology study examining STI rates and risk factors. Uses PCR for diagnosis but does not evaluate a rapid POC test. No diagnostic accuracy comparison or 2x2 data.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating a rapid POC test in sex workers attending STI clinics. Compares with PCR as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (62.96%) and specificity (99.60%). All 278 participants received both tests. Provides 2x2 data. Sex workers are nonpregnant women of reproductive age.
This is a review article discussing available diagnostic tests. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. No original data or 2x2 tables.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating the Chlamydia Rapid Test (POC) with vaginal swabs in women aged 16-54 at sexual health clinics. Compares with PCR and SDA as reference standards. Reports sensitivity (83.5%/81.6%), specificity (98.9%/98.3%), PPV, and NPV. All 1349 women received both index test and reference standard. Provides 2x2 data.

This study examines serovar distribution and associations with clinical symptoms, not diagnostic accuracy. Uses PCR for genotyping but does not evaluate a rapid POC test. No 2x2 data for diagnostic accuracy.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating the Chlamydia Rapid Test (CRT) POC in women at STI clinics. Compares with NAAT (Aptima) as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (41.2%) and specificity (96.4%). All 912 women received both tests. Provides 2x2 data.
This is a review article about immune mechanisms and infertility related to Chlamydia. Not a diagnostic accuracy study. No POC test evaluation or 2x2 data.
This is a methodological paper about search strategies for systematic reviews. Not a diagnostic accuracy study. No POC test evaluation or 2x2 data.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating a chlamydial optical immunoassay (OIA) rapid POC test. Compares with LCR as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (31.6%) and specificity (98.9%). All 415 outpatients received both tests. Provides 2x2 data.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating three POC tests (Handilab-C, Biorapid CHLAMYDIA Ag, QuickVue Chlamydia) in women at an STI clinic. Compares with NAAT as reference standard. Reports sensitivities (17%, 27%, 12%). All 772 women received both index tests and reference standard. Provides 2x2 data.
This is a review article examining risk factors for chlamydial infection. Not a diagnostic accuracy study. No POC test evaluation or 2x2 data.
This is a guideline document for laboratory diagnosis. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. No original data or 2x2 tables.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating a prototype POC test device in adolescent women. Compares with cervical NAAT as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (38% initial, 80% improved) and discusses specificity issues. All participants received both index test and reference standard. Provides 2x2 data for diagnostic accuracy assessment.
This is a study about treatment outcomes and patient follow-up compliance, not diagnostic accuracy. Uses retrospective chart review. No POC test evaluation or 2x2 data for diagnostic accuracy.
